paper.citation: Athey, S., Imbens, G. W. and Wager, S. (2018). Approximate residual balancing: Debiased inference of average treatment effects in high dimensions. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Statistical Methodology), 80(4), 597-623. DOI: 10.1111/rssb.12268.
paper.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Statistical Methodology)
paper.source_locator: Section 5.2, paragraph headed by the unnumbered “moderately sparse two-stage” simulation description; electronic reprint PDF page 22/27 (printed page 618) for the shifted-index and treatment-logistic definition. Coefficient shapes are in the equation labelled eq:betas in Section 5.2, PDF page 21/27 (printed page 617), with dense/harmonic/moderately sparse/very sparse definitions. Table 4 and its footnote: PDF page 23/27 (printed page 619), n=600, p=2000, ||beta_Y||_2=1, 400 replications, rho in {0.5,0.9}. The equation is not assigned a visible numbered equation in the reprint; paragraph and source label are used instead. Author software repository https://github.com/swager/balanceHD was cited in the article, but no repository code commit was used or claimed.

mechanism.name: Moderately sparse two-stage ATE DGP with index-shifted outcome coefficients

generation_equations.label: Covariates
generation_equations.expression: X_i ~ Normal_p(0,Sigma), Sigma_ij=rho^|i-j|; rho in {0.5,0.9}, p=2000.

generation_equations.label: Equivalent Gaussian recursion used in implementation
generation_equations.expression: X_i1=Z_i1; X_ij=rho*X_i,j-1 + sqrt(1-rho^2)*Z_ij for j=2,...,p, where innovations Z_ij are iid Normal(0,1). This is distributionally equivalent to the source covariance, not the same random draw sequence.

generation_equations.label: Index permutation
generation_equations.expression: k_j = (23*(j-1)) mod p. Construct raw profile b_{k_j} according to one of the four source profiles, then beta_Y=raw/sqrt(sum_j raw_j^2), so ||beta_Y||_2=1.

generation_equations.label: Moderately sparse outcome profile
generation_equations.expression: raw_j=10 if k_j<10; raw_j=1 if 10<=k_j<100; raw_j=0 if k_j>=100; k_j=(23*(j-1)) mod p.

generation_equations.label: Very sparse outcome profile
generation_equations.expression: raw_j=1 if k_j<10, otherwise 0; k_j=(23*(j-1)) mod p.

generation_equations.label: Treatment assignment
generation_equations.expression: W_i | X_i ~ Bernoulli(expit(sum_{j=1}^{100} X_ij/40)); equivalently P(W_i=1|X_i)=1/[1+exp(-sum_{j=1}^{100} X_ij/40)].

generation_equations.label: Observed outcome
generation_equations.expression: Y_i = X_i^T beta_Y + 0.5 W_i + epsilon_i, epsilon_i ~ Normal(0,1), independent under the implementation convention.

generation_equations.label: Target / potential outcomes
generation_equations.expression: Y_i(w)=X_i^T beta_Y + 0.5w + epsilon_i, w in {0,1}; ATE=E[Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)]=0.5.

evidence.expression: X_ij=rho*X_i,j-1 + sqrt(1-rho^2)*Z_ij for j=2,...,p, where innovations Z_ij are iid Normal(0,1). This is distributionally equivalent to the source covariance, not the same random draw sequence.

sampling.dependence: Individuals are independent. Within each individual, X coordinates have AR(1) Gaussian correlation Sigma_ij=rho^|i-j|. W depends on the first 100 X coordinates through a logistic link. Outcome noise is independent across individuals and independent of X and W by implementation assumption; no interference.

assumptions: Consistency: the observed outcome equals Y(W).

The structural outcome error is independent of pretreatment X and treatment assignment W under this implementation, so conditional exchangeability holds given the full X vector; the complete cross-independence statement is not fully enumerated in the source paragraph and remains for scientific review.
For every finite X the specified logistic probability is strictly between 0 and 1; because the Gaussian support is unbounded, no uniform propensity-score bound away from 0 and 1 is claimed.
Individuals are independently sampled from the superpopulation; there is no interference.

properties.notes: Table 4 uses n=600 and p=2000 (p>n), with rho=0.5 or 0.9. The outcome beta profile is one of dense, harmonic, moderately sparse, or very sparse, with source-specified 23-mod-p index shift, normalized to l2 norm 1. Active outcome coefficients by profile: dense=2000, harmonic=2000, moderately_sparse=100, very_sparse=10. Treatment assignment is nonlinear through expit(sum_{j=1}^{100} X_ij / 40); no interaction product terms occur in the equations.

estimand.name: ATE
estimand.definition: Population average treatment effect E[Y(1)-Y(0)] under the Section 5.2 moderately sparse two-stage DGP, comparing the intervention W=1 with W=0 while holding the same pretreatment X and outcome disturbance fixed.

truth.expression: Population average treatment effect E[Y(1)-Y(0)] under the Section 5.2 moderately sparse two-stage DGP, comparing the intervention W=1 with W=0 while holding the same pretreatment X and outcome disturbance fixed.
truth.derivation: Analytical potential-outcome contrast. From Y(w)=X^T beta_Y + 0.5*w + epsilon, Y(1)-Y(0)=0.5 for every X and common epsilon, hence population ATE=0.5. estimated_error=0 because no numerical integration or Monte Carlo truth approximation is used.

adaptations: Generate the AR(1)-correlated Gaussian covariates by the equivalent Gaussian innovation recursion; this preserves the specified joint distribution but not the authors’ random-number sequence.
Implement the paper-specified index permutation k_j = 23*(j-1) mod p in zero-based array form, then normalize each outcome coefficient profile to the Table 4 norm ||beta_Y||_2=1.
Make the ATE target explicit through the potential-outcome representation Y(w)=X^T beta_Y + 0.5*w + epsilon, implied by the source outcome equation.

For executable sampling, draw outcome errors independently of X and W and across individuals; the two-stage paragraph specifies standard Gaussian outcome noise but does not enumerate every cross-independence relation. This additional independence convention is pending scientific confirmation.
